verification.fact_verification_explanation: The customer's central allegation is that the 60-days-past-due credit reporting is wrong because they never missed a payment in 18 months. The records contradict this. The reporting did happen: on 2026-04-20 the account was reported to the credit bureaus as 60 days past due. But the transaction log shows the 2026-03-18 and 2026-04-18 scheduled installments of $140.00 were both not received. Payments of $140.00 were received on 2026-01-18 and 2026-02-18. The missed installments were not cured until 2026-05-18, when a $280.00 payment covering 2 installments was received. The 2026-06-18 installment was also received, and the account now shows as current. The customer is right that the account was reported as 60 days past due, but wrong that no payments were missed. The customer's bank statements are not on file, but the company's own records directly contradict the claim. Note for the reviewer: the log shows the oldest missed installment (2026-03-18) was about 33 days old on 2026-04-20, so the reviewer may want to confirm how the '60 days past due' status was derived. The log shows two missed installments but does not explain the status code.
verification.risk_rationale: There is no attorney/regulator reference, identity-theft dispute, misleading-terms allegation, collector-conduct allegation, hardship or vulnerability indicator, and no dollar amount over $200 is at issue (installments are $140); the claim is confirmed false against clear payment records.

policy.text:
# Policy: Credit Reporting Disputes (Fair Credit Reporting Act)

**Applies to:** Any complaint alleging inaccurate, incomplete, or unverifiable information reported to a consumer reporting agency (credit bureau).

## Requirements
- As a furnisher of information, we must investigate a dispute (received either directly from the consumer or relayed by a credit bureau) within **30 days**, extendable to **45 days** if the consumer provides additional information during the 30-day window.
- We must review all relevant information provided by the consumer, correct any inaccuracy found, and report the results of the investigation back to the consumer and, if applicable, to the credit bureau.
- If an item is found to be inaccurate or unverifiable, it must be corrected or deleted from our reporting **promptly**.
- We may not resume reporting an item we previously deleted unless we can certify the information is accurate and complete.
- A consumer may request a statement of the dispute to be included in their credit file if the dispute is not resolved to their satisfaction.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May confirm whether our internal records match or contradict what is reported (e.g., payment history, account status).
- May state the applicable 30/45-day investigation timeline.
- May NOT promise a specific bureau will update within a specific number of days — we control our own furnishing, not the bureau's processing timeline.

## Escalation trigger
A **third or subsequent dispute on the same item**, or any complaint stating an investigation was closed with no explanation of what was actually checked, should be escalated — repeated unresolved disputes carry elevated regulatory risk.

## Remedy authority
Front-line staff may initiate a correction to our own furnished data (status, balance, payment history) when the internal transaction record clearly supports the correction. Removing an account entirely, or correcting identity-mismatch issues, requires supervisor or fraud-team review.

*Source: Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1681 et seq. Generic, illustrative summary for internal training/demo purposes, not legal advice.*

draft.draft_text:
Thank you for writing to us about the 60 days past due status showing on your credit report. We understand how upsetting it is to see that when you've told us you've never missed a payment and your bank statements show every payment made on time for the past 18 months.

We went through the payment history on your account. Here's what we found on each point you raised.

The 60 days past due status: Our records show the account was reported to the credit bureaus as 60 days past due on April 20, 2026. The records we have don't show how that status was worked out, so we can't explain how it was calculated.

Never missing a payment: Our records show something different from what you've described. We received your $140.00 installments on January 18 and February 18, 2026. We did not receive the installments due on March 18 and April 18, 2026. On May 18, 2026, we received a $280.00 payment covering those two installments. The June 18 installment was received as well, and your account now shows as current.

Payments on time for the past 18 months: We don't have your bank statements, so we haven't been able to compare them with our records. The payment history we do have is the one described above.

Where this leaves things: Based on our records, we haven't found a payment error, so we haven't made any change to what's being reported on your account. That isn't the end of the road. If your bank statements show the March and April 2026 payments leaving your account, please send them to us. You can send them, or anything else you think is relevant, at any time, and we will review it.

For credit reporting disputes, we investigate within 30 days. That can extend to 45 days if you send us additional information during that time. We can't tell you when a credit bureau will update its file, because that happens on the bureau's own timeline. If the dispute isn't resolved to your satisfaction, you can ask for a statement of your dispute to be included in your credit file.

You can reply to this message or call us at the number on your account. Case reference: 23623033.

verifier.groundedness_check: pass — every date and amount traces to the verification output: $140.00 installments received 1/18 and 2/18, 3/18 and 4/18 not received, $280.00 received 5/18 covering two installments, 6/18 received, account now current, and the 60-day status reported on 4/20/2026. The 30/45-day timeline and the dispute-statement option come from Policy 04. The draft states plainly that it cannot explain how the 60-day status was derived, which matches the reviewer note. Reviewer note, not a failure: the verification output flags that the oldest missed installment was only about 33 days old on 4/20, so the human reviewer should confirm the 60-day status before sending. The draft makes no claim that the status is correct.
verifier.policy_authorization_check: pass — remedy_stated and referral_stated are both null, and no refund, correction, or other remedy is promised, so nothing exceeds Policy 04 authority.
verifier.prohibited_language_check: pass — no fault admission beyond confirmed fact, no future guarantees, no legal conclusions, and no promised remedies. The draft invites the customer to send bank statements and states it cannot control bureau timing. Nothing discourages other channels.
verifier.tone_structure_check: pass — the draft follows Policy 11: acknowledgment that references the specific issue, findings addressed per allegation, outcome (no change, with an explanation), next steps, then the case reference 23623033. The tone is plain and non-performative, with no marketing content. One paragraph runs to five sentences against the 2-4 guideline, which is minor and does not affect the structure.
